newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway gives go-ahead for first gas power stations.
newsitem.headline: Norway gives go-ahead for first gas power stations.

text.p: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Administration (NVE) said on Wednesday it had given Naturkraft AS the go-ahead for the construction of the country's first gas-fired power stations.

The two 350 megawatt gas power plants will produce around 5.6 terrawatt hours per year. One will be built at Kaarstoe and the other at Kollsnes, both in the southwest of the country, at a cost of 3.6 billion crowns.

Naturkraft, set up specifically for the gas plant project, is a joint-venture between Norsk Hydro ASA, Norway's largest electricity producer Statkraft A/S and state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap A/S.
NVE said the two plants were expected to raise Norwegian emissions of carbon dioxide by 2.1 million tonnes per year.
Until now, Norway has relied exclusively on hydroelectricity for its own production or on imports from Denmark and Sweden.
Norwegian electricity prices reached record highs this year due to extremely low rain and snow fall last winter which left extremely low water levels in reservoirs.
Naturkraft says the combination of hydropower and gas-fired stations will lay the ground for stable electricity supply agreements with Sweden and Finland.
In January Norway and Sweden opened a joint electricity trading exchange where power from both countries can be bought and sold like any other commodity.
Finland is expected to join its two neighbours next year, while Danish participation will require more time due to domestic legislation.
